scope: Primary methodological sources for a polished misleading representation, independent checking evidence, and a disclosed correction/debrief.
execution_policy: Read-only primary-source review; no implementation, browser study, deployment, recruitment, human-participant work, or invented susceptibility outcomes.

primary_sources.title: The Persuasive Power of Data Visualization
primary_sources.publisher: IEEE Transactions on Visualization and Computer Graphics, 20(12), 2211-2220
primary_sources.source_type: peer-reviewed empirical journal article; publisher DOI primary attribution and author-associated full-paper copy
claims_used: Randomized crowd-sourced experiments compared charts and tables in messages designed to change attitudes.
Charts were more persuasive than tables under some initial-attitude conditions, while the result varied with topic and prior attitude.
The authors leave the causal mechanism of medium effects unresolved.
primary_sources.gate13_use: Motivate a polished-view counterexample with fixed underlying facts and separate logs for the initial representation, checking evidence, and later correction.
primary_sources.limits: Human attitude-change study with selected topics and treatments; it does not show that geometry persuades, that a wrong view fools users, or that the result transfers to this fixture.

primary_sources.title: Debunking misleading graphs effectively: How vocationally educated young adults perceive graphs
primary_sources.source_type: peer-reviewed open-access empirical research article; publisher full text and DOI
claims_used: The study used fictional misleading and accurate graphs, including truncated axes, distorted pictorial areas, and 3D pies.
The survey (n=130) and think-aloud interviews (n=10) evaluated clean versus full-design corrections.
The article reports reduced misleading effects after correction and no detected clean/full correction difference, with learning limited to new graphs of the same type.
primary_sources.gate13_use: Require an accurate comparator or checking record, a typed mismatch explanation, and a separately logged disclosed correction/debrief while preserving the original misleading artifact.
primary_sources.limits: Specific graph types, fictional data, vocationally educated young-adult sample, and disclosed preregistration-analysis deviations; no basis for a Looking Glass human or debiasing claim.

derived_gate13_requirements.design: Freeze source facts and the correct answer independently, then verify that the polished representation makes a different claim without changing the underlying facts.
derived_gate13_requirements.basis: Pandey et al. (2014); Wijnker et al. (2026)

derived_gate13_requirements.design: Expose source facts, derivation, mismatch description, and an accurate comparator through the same public fixture routes; do not silently alter the original view.
derived_gate13_requirements.basis: Wijnker et al. (2026) correction design; Gate13 scope

derived_gate13_requirements.design: Record correction as a distinct state that identifies the wrong encoding or inference and points to existing evidence without adding facts or deleting the misleading artifact.
Report only software mismatch, evidence-access, and correction-path checks; reserve persuasion, resistance, confidence, and debiasing claims for an approved human protocol.
derived_gate13_requirements.basis: Both primary studies and the Gate13 evidence boundary

limits: Both sources are human empirical studies with specific populations, topics, graph forms, and procedures; their findings do not establish effects in the public synthetic fixture.

The Gate13 software result is limited to independently verified mismatch, equal evidence access, and disclosed correction/debrief state; it makes no persuasion, resistance, confidence-calibration, or successful-debiasing claim.
Wijnker et al. disclose deviations from preregistered analysis and limit the learning result to new misleading graphs of the same type.
